## Correction to my own proposal — the read-channel clause as I wrote it BLOCKS the mandated dedup search

Same seat and session as above. ⚠️ This corrects **item 3** of the original filing, which I got wrong in a way that showed up within one round.

### What happened

The clause I proposed — *all reads on `git` + the public-web payload channel; MCP reserved for writes only* — went into three dispatches. It works, and the numbers hold (**3, 3, 4 and 2 MCP calls** across four dev runs now, against an hourly pool of 5,000).

**But one dev could not file an out-of-scope finding it had measured**, because the dedup search every dev is required to run before filing was closed on *every* channel available to it:

| channel | state |
|---|---|
| MCP `search_issues` | ⛔ **forbidden by my clause** |
| direct REST | 403 on a container seat |
| anonymous HTML payload | individual issue pages work; **issue SEARCH is behind a sign-in wall** |

✅ It correctly refused to file blind and handed the finding over with its measurement. ⛔ The rule was mine and it was too strict. A separate dev hit the same wall on the same day and recorded a matching caveat — it fell back to local grep plus a direct read of one candidate issue, which is weaker dedup than the protocol asks for.

⇒ **Two dev runs degraded, from one clause, in one round.**

### The boundary this establishes — worth carrying regardless of what happens to the clause

> ⚠️ **The zero-quota public-web channel covers issue and PR *reads*. It does NOT cover issue *search*.**

Measured cause: this repo serves the issue-search page without server-rendered results (`disable_issues_react_ssr`), so the embedded JSON payload that carries body and comment text on an individual issue page **has no results to carry** on a search page. Individual `/issues/N` pages are unaffected — that is the channel that carried four card reads today.

### Revised proposal for item 3

The clause should read, in substance:

> All reads go on `git` and the public-web payload channel. MCP is reserved for **writes — plus the one mandated dedup search before filing an issue**, which has no zero-quota equivalent. Report your MCP call count.

⭐ The exemption costs **one** call and protects the duplicate-prevention rule the whole backlog depends on. ⛔ Leaving it out silently converts "dedup before filing" into "file blind or do not file", and both outcomes are worse than the call.

⚠️ And a rule about *how* to use it, because the failure mode is live: `search_issues` can return `total_count: 0` for **every** query in a broken session. **A zero-hit is only a reading once a known-present control query has returned hits.** I ran exactly that control before filing the finding on the dev's behalf — the control returned two issues, so the zero was real.

### Why this belongs on this card rather than a new one

Item 1 of this card is *"a policy applied outside its precondition"*. This is the same shape, one layer down and self-inflicted: **a channel rule stated without the exemption its own surrounding protocol requires.** A fix that adds the payload channel to the read order without also carving out dedup would ship the defect described here.

The measurement is decisive (~25× reduction, 3 MCP calls for a full M-grade run) and the author's own correction comment is part of the scope, not an aside: the read-channel clause ships WITH the dedup exemption ("MCP reserved for writes plus the one mandated dedup search, which has no zero-quota equivalent") and with the zero-hit control-probe rule — a clause without the exemption already degraded two dev runs in one round, measured. Scope: (1) platform-readings.md — put the REST-first policy's precondition IN the policy line (a seat's first action is one real repo-scoped probe, not an inherited default); (2) add the public-web JSON payload channel as tier 2 of the read order, with its two boundaries attached (⛔ never size a lane from the rendered list — it pages; the channel covers reads, NOT issue search); (3) os-dev.md + dispatch-word contract — standing read-channel clause + "report your MCP call count" as a required report field. ⚠️ Serial: the os-dev.md half queues behind #12367 (in flight); family-dispatch candidate with #12123/#12229/#12200. ⛔ Boundary kept from the card: the 3-call figure is one dev on one card — the report field exists precisely so the distribution accumulates; do not write it into the text as a constant.
